Methods describe TNM stage I (T1-2N0M0) eligibility, while Table I lists TNM I/IIa/IIb. Exact 24-h pain values are graph-only; rescue-tramadol quantities and the complication ascertainment window are not reported.
Retain arm counts and directly reported outcomes as source truth; flag staging discrepancy; do not infer graph values or a 0–24 h PONV window.
Source-direct addition / distribution and blinding QC

Exact 0–24 h sufentanil pump dose is reported as median/IQR, not mean/SD. Only 72.2% vs 71.0% received a sufentanil analgesic pump, so zeros are retained in the reported group distribution. Patients could not be fully blinded because true TEAS was perceptible; subjective pain/PONV outcomes therefore need outcome-specific RoB consideration.

Retain the reported median/IQR and full ITT denominators; do not convert to mean/SD without a prespecified method. Use raw events/total for binary outcomes. Keep the selected RoB 2 assessment specific to the objective 24-h opioid result.
Material for analysis-method / outcome-specific RoB QC
Source-direct addition / missing 24-h opioid + attrition/companion-publication QC

Exact cumulative 0–24 h postoperative sufentanil consumption is not reported. The postoperative pump had a fixed basal infusion plus patient-triggered boluses, so the basal component alone is not total opioid exposure. Four randomized patients (2/group) were excluded using post-randomization duration/blood-loss criteria that are related to anesthetic consumption. The same research group previously published an EA supratentorial-craniotomy trial (An 2014); the present source describes that work as previous research and uses a distinct TEAS protocol/sample, but cohort overlap is not directly demonstrated or excluded.

Exclude Liu 2015 from the strict 0–24 h postoperative opioid model unless author/raw data provide total pump consumption. Retain exact intraoperative sufentanil and recovery outcomes. Treat POD pain as graph-only and POD nausea/vomiting as day-labelled. Keep the possible relationship to An 2014 as an identity-QC note, not a duplicate hold, unless source-level overlap is demonstrated.
Material for primary-outcome availability / result-specific RoB / publication-family QC

Three-arm trial was not blinded. One of 16 randomized TAES participants was excluded after randomization for non-protocol drug use. Primary review-relevant 0–24 h tramadol PCA is reported, but rescue IM pethidine is also reported separately; a combined total-opioid mean/SD cannot be derived without covariance/raw data. Methods describe VAS as 1–10 while tables include values of 0.

Retain TAES-vs-control and TAES-vs-incision-TENS as correlated contrasts from one RCT. Keep 0–24 h tramadol conditional for total-opioid synthesis, retain pethidine as a separate rescue-opioid outcome, and preserve the VAS scale inconsistency as source QC. Do not infer unreported PONV group values.
Source-direct integration / PCA-device semantics / ITT-PP handling

The trial randomized 85 patients and states that all 85 were included in the ITT population, while 78 formed the PP population. Table 3 reports outcomes using the original 42/43 group denominators. PCA outcome is reported as pump-press number. Methods state each press resulted in a 2-mL infusion from 4 mg butorphanol + 2 g propacetamol/100 mL, but a 15-min lockout was also programmed; this creates ambiguity about whether every counted press is necessarily a delivered bolus. Butorphanol also requires an explicitly prespecified cross-drug conversion rule before any MME pooling.

Retain 42/43 for source-reported ITT Table 3 results. Keep PCA presses as the direct endpoint. If calculating the butorphanol component, label it derived/conditional (0.08 mg per reported press) and do not enter the strict total-opioid model unless device semantics and the review's butorphanol conversion rule are prespecified.
Material for opioid-definition / device-outcome / result-specific RoB QC
Source-direct integration / three-arm comparator handling / selective-reporting QC

The trial has one TEAS arm and two controls (no-current sham and PCA-only), so both contrasts share the same TEAS participants and must not be counted as independent studies. The exact 0–24 h primary morphine endpoint is reported with both mean/SD and median/IQR. Participants were blinded, but personnel were not; the complete prespecified analysis plan was not supplied. In addition, the source is internally inconsistent about surgical approach: the inclusion criteria specify elective laparoscopic mesh inguinal hernia repair, while the anesthesia/surgery section states the Lichtenstein tension-free method.

Select TEAS-vs-sham as the principal simple-pairwise primary opioid contrast; retain TEAS-vs-PCA-only as a correlated supportive/usual-care contrast. Use the directly reported mean/SD for the strict primary continuous dataset and preserve median/IQR as supporting distribution information. Keep result-specific RoB 2 as Some concerns. Record inguinal hernia repair as the surgery type, but leave laparoscopic-versus-open surgical approach unresolved until the protocol/registry or authors clarify the discrepancy.
Material for multi-arm handling / primary-outcome QC
Source-direct integration / graph-only outcomes / internal denominator-age inconsistencies

Key clinical recovery and pain results are shown in Figure 2 as bar graphs with mean±SE and are not numerically tabulated. The paper reports percentage reductions and P values but not exact group means/SEs. Text reports prolonged ileus (>96 h to defecation) in 5 sham patients and none in TEA, whereas Table 2 classifies 33 non-endpoint and 11 endpoint patients (44 total) despite only 42 randomized. The abstract reports mean age 69.5±1.5 years, while Table 1 reports 64.0±2.6 and 68.0±1.4 years by group.

Retain exact narrative percentages/P values and the textual 0/21 vs 5/21 ileus statement as source truth, but do not pool graph-only continuous outcomes without formal digitization. Keep the binary ileus row on source-QC hold until the Table 2 denominator inconsistency is adjudicated. Use Table 1 arm-specific demographics rather than the incompatible abstract age for covariates.

V34_Study_Summary: Drive search did not return a standalone supplementary file. Main article references Supplemental Tables 1–2 for ITT PON/POV analyses. Main-table extraction is per-protocol. Randomized arm sizes conflict between abstract and CONSORT figure.
59 randomized (30/29), 57 completed/analyzed (29/28). Rescue medication defined as bucinnazine 100 mg IM if VAS >3; exact rescue time window not attached to Table 3.

Paper has a participant-flow inconsistency: Methods mention 120 women, while abstract/results report 105 in the final study cohort (52/53). NRS is described in Results as measured in the mobile state. Table 7 parenthetical NRS statistic is not explicitly defined.

Main paper references multiple Supplemental Digital Contents; no standalone supplement was located in Drive in the current search. Major internal 24-h QoR-15 conflict between Results prose and Table 3; table values retained and conflict flagged.
All six requested VAS≥4/PONV assessment timepoints are printed in Table 5. Analysis population is not explicitly labelled ITT/per-protocol in the publication.

117/120 completed (L-TEAS 58, C-TEAS 59). Exact VAS at 4/8/24 h is printed; 16/36 h are graph-only. Figure 5 gives PONV counts 7 vs 19. Satisfaction prose conflicts with Table 4. The 24-h PCIA point is graph-only and represents multimodal PCIA solution volume, not a printed exact sufentanil mass.

Randomized 51 vs 50; analyzed 43 vs 45. Source directly reports VAS and I-FEED at 24/48/72 h, QoR-40 at discharge, LOS, vomiting, additional ketorolac use and bowel obstruction. Results prose says QoR-40 was lower with EA, but Table 4 shows 196 vs 192; the table direction is preserved and the conflict is flagged.

610 randomized/analyzed (303 TEAS, 307 sham). Table III provides bowel-sound recovery plus abdominal pain, distention, nausea and vomiting-episode data. The main paper states no difference in 30-day complications or total LOS but directs exact values to Supplementary Table S4; those exact supplemental values are therefore SOURCE NOT ACCESSED, not NOT REPORTED.

Secondary outcomes use PP n=294 vs 293; first-flatus ITT also exists separately. First defecation, abdominal distention, hospital cost, LOS and adverse events are directly printed. One NRS summary is printed without identifying whether it is the planned 6-, 24- or 48-h assessment; retained as AMBIGUOUS. Printed effect direction/CI oddities are preserved verbatim.

Randomized 43 vs 45; analyzed 40 vs 43. POD3 PSQI/AIS and rest/activity VAS trajectories are graph-only where exact values are not printed; no visual digitization was performed. LOS and adverse-event counts are directly tabulated.

120 randomized; 115 analyzed (57 TEAS, 58 sham). Actual PDF confirms missing 0–2 h vomiting, nausea severity at all three intervals, early pain, metoclopramide rescue and zero TEAS AEs. The Results prose contains a typo for 2–6 h vomiting (P=0.47) while Table 3 and abstract report P=0.047; table value is authoritative for extraction.

380 randomized (95/arm); 361 analyzed: SSS 90, TSS 91, TTS 91, TST 89. Exact 1/6/48 h pain values are not printed and are retained GRAPH ONLY. Table 2 provides percentage/95%CI data for nausea, vomiting, rescue antiemetic and satisfaction; raw event counts were not reconstructed. Table 2 also gives arm-specific intraoperative opioid, extubation, PACU, flatus and defecation results.

90 randomized/analyzed (30/group). Table 2 gives mean VAS over 24 h plus PONV/drowsiness/pruritus percentages. Individual 6-hourly VAS values are not numerically printed. Figure 3 gives interval morphine trajectories; exact non-6–12 h values are graph-only. Source provides exact Group III 6–12 h morphine and alfentanil values missing from v33.

Three-arm multicenter trial: sham 188, single-PC6 198, combined PC6+CV17 190. Main PDF directly supplies 24-h rest/cough NRS, rescue parecoxib, nausea, vomiting, PONV severity, satisfaction, immediate recovery, and 3/6-month pain data. There are internal P-value conflicts between Table 3 and Results prose for rest NRS, cough NRS and rescue analgesia; both are preserved.

60 randomized, 53 analyzed. Table 7 gives 48-h VAS and LOS; Tables 5–6 give recovery and adverse-event data; Table 2 gives POD7 PND. Important source inconsistency: abstract reports 24-h EA VAS 2.65±0.94, whereas Table 7 reports 2.78±0.97; v33 uses the Table 7 value. PND percentages imply different denominators from the study-level analyzed group sizes and must remain flagged.

140 randomized by NVP-risk stratum; analyzed SNVP-ODT 33/35 and SNVP-OD 35/35, MNVP 35/35 per subgroup. Table 3 supplies all interval PONV counts. A combined 0–6 h vomiting comparison is printed for the SNVP stratum. Pain VAS was prespecified at the same postoperative assessment times but numerical pain results are not reported.

88 randomized, 85 completed (42 TEAS, 43 control). Source directly reports interval nausea/vomiting, remifentanil, PCIA use, pain, PSQI, GI recovery, LOS and adverse reactions. QoR-40 6/24 h is figure-only; 48-h means are printed but exact SDs are not. Internal conflict: 24-h pain P=0.042 in prose but bP=0.422 in Table 4 footnote.

60 randomized/analyzed, 30/group. POD2 QoR-40, PONV, rescue tropisetron and MMSE are missing from v33. Internal source conflicts: abstract gives TEAS pain SD 1.41/0.88 whereas Table 2 gives 1.53/0.98; Results prose says POD2 pain P=0.26 while Table 2 marks *P<0.05 and abstract calls both timepoints significant.

80 assessed, 75 randomized (TEAS 37, control 38), 70 analyzed (35/group). v33 has reversed randomized-arm counts in its CRBD rows (38/37 instead of TEAS37/control38). Table 1 supplies intraoperative sufentanil/remifentanil. Table 4 supplies PONV, an ambiguously defined pain-event row, MMSE, QoR and extra analgesia. Major source conflict: abstract reports 48-h CRBD 4/35 vs7/35, whereas Table 2 prints 4/35 vs19/35; v33 currently uses the table value 19.

study_summary.note: Drive search did not return a standalone supplementary file. Main article references Supplemental Tables 1–2 for ITT PON/POV analyses. Main-table extraction is per-protocol. Randomized arm sizes conflict between abstract and CONSORT figure.
59 randomized (30/29), 57 completed/analyzed (29/28). Rescue medication defined as bucinnazine 100 mg IM if VAS >3; exact rescue time window not attached to Table 3.

Paper has a participant-flow inconsistency: Methods mention 120 women, while abstract/results report 105 in the final study cohort (52/53). NRS is described in Results as measured in the mobile state. Table 7 parenthetical NRS statistic is not explicitly defined.

Main paper references multiple Supplemental Digital Contents; no standalone supplement was located in Drive in the current search. Major internal 24-h QoR-15 conflict between Results prose and Table 3; table values retained and conflict flagged.
All six requested VAS≥4/PONV assessment timepoints are printed in Table 5. Analysis population is not explicitly labelled ITT/per-protocol in the publication.

117/120 completed (L-TEAS 58, C-TEAS 59). Exact VAS at 4/8/24 h is printed; 16/36 h are graph-only. Figure 5 gives PONV counts 7 vs 19. Satisfaction prose conflicts with Table 4. The 24-h PCIA point is graph-only and represents multimodal PCIA solution volume, not a printed exact sufentanil mass.

Randomized 51 vs 50; analyzed 43 vs 45. Source directly reports VAS and I-FEED at 24/48/72 h, QoR-40 at discharge, LOS, vomiting, additional ketorolac use and bowel obstruction. Results prose says QoR-40 was lower with EA, but Table 4 shows 196 vs 192; the table direction is preserved and the conflict is flagged.

610 randomized/analyzed (303 TEAS, 307 sham). Table III provides bowel-sound recovery plus abdominal pain, distention, nausea and vomiting-episode data. The main paper states no difference in 30-day complications or total LOS but directs exact values to Supplementary Table S4; those exact supplemental values are therefore SOURCE NOT ACCESSED, not NOT REPORTED.

Secondary outcomes use PP n=294 vs 293; first-flatus ITT also exists separately. First defecation, abdominal distention, hospital cost, LOS and adverse events are directly printed. One NRS summary is printed without identifying whether it is the planned 6-, 24- or 48-h assessment; retained as AMBIGUOUS. Printed effect direction/CI oddities are preserved verbatim.

Randomized 43 vs 45; analyzed 40 vs 43. POD3 PSQI/AIS and rest/activity VAS trajectories are graph-only where exact values are not printed; no visual digitization was performed. LOS and adverse-event counts are directly tabulated.

120 randomized; 115 analyzed (57 TEAS, 58 sham). Actual PDF confirms missing 0–2 h vomiting, nausea severity at all three intervals, early pain, metoclopramide rescue and zero TEAS AEs. The Results prose contains a typo for 2–6 h vomiting (P=0.47) while Table 3 and abstract report P=0.047; table value is authoritative for extraction.

380 randomized (95/arm); 361 analyzed: SSS 90, TSS 91, TTS 91, TST 89. Exact 1/6/48 h pain values are not printed and are retained GRAPH ONLY. Table 2 provides percentage/95%CI data for nausea, vomiting, rescue antiemetic and satisfaction; raw event counts were not reconstructed. Table 2 also gives arm-specific intraoperative opioid, extubation, PACU, flatus and defecation results.

90 randomized/analyzed (30/group). Table 2 gives mean VAS over 24 h plus PONV/drowsiness/pruritus percentages. Individual 6-hourly VAS values are not numerically printed. Figure 3 gives interval morphine trajectories; exact non-6–12 h values are graph-only. Source provides exact Group III 6–12 h morphine and alfentanil values missing from v33.

Three-arm multicenter trial: sham 188, single-PC6 198, combined PC6+CV17 190. Main PDF directly supplies 24-h rest/cough NRS, rescue parecoxib, nausea, vomiting, PONV severity, satisfaction, immediate recovery, and 3/6-month pain data. There are internal P-value conflicts between Table 3 and Results prose for rest NRS, cough NRS and rescue analgesia; both are preserved.

60 randomized, 53 analyzed. Table 7 gives 48-h VAS and LOS; Tables 5–6 give recovery and adverse-event data; Table 2 gives POD7 PND. Important source inconsistency: abstract reports 24-h EA VAS 2.65±0.94, whereas Table 7 reports 2.78±0.97; v33 uses the Table 7 value. PND percentages imply different denominators from the study-level analyzed group sizes and must remain flagged.

140 randomized by NVP-risk stratum; analyzed SNVP-ODT 33/35 and SNVP-OD 35/35, MNVP 35/35 per subgroup. Table 3 supplies all interval PONV counts. A combined 0–6 h vomiting comparison is printed for the SNVP stratum. Pain VAS was prespecified at the same postoperative assessment times but numerical pain results are not reported.

88 randomized, 85 completed (42 TEAS, 43 control). Source directly reports interval nausea/vomiting, remifentanil, PCIA use, pain, PSQI, GI recovery, LOS and adverse reactions. QoR-40 6/24 h is figure-only; 48-h means are printed but exact SDs are not. Internal conflict: 24-h pain P=0.042 in prose but bP=0.422 in Table 4 footnote.

60 randomized/analyzed, 30/group. POD2 QoR-40, PONV, rescue tropisetron and MMSE are missing from v33. Internal source conflicts: abstract gives TEAS pain SD 1.41/0.88 whereas Table 2 gives 1.53/0.98; Results prose says POD2 pain P=0.26 while Table 2 marks *P<0.05 and abstract calls both timepoints significant.

80 assessed, 75 randomized (TEAS 37, control 38), 70 analyzed (35/group). v33 has reversed randomized-arm counts in its CRBD rows (38/37 instead of TEAS37/control38). Table 1 supplies intraoperative sufentanil/remifentanil. Table 4 supplies PONV, an ambiguously defined pain-event row, MMSE, QoR and extra analgesia. Major source conflict: abstract reports 48-h CRBD 4/35 vs7/35, whereas Table 2 prints 4/35 vs19/35; v33 currently uses the table value 19.
